\section*{Abstract}
\logpage{[ 0, 0, 1 ]}
 The package implements the algorithms of Parker and Semeraro (\cite{PS21}) for saturated fusion systems on finite $p$-groups in GAP 4: construction of fusion systems from generating automizers
and from finite groups, computation of $F$-conjugacy classes and automizers, a saturation test, the isomorphism test and
the classification of all saturated fusion systems on a given $p$-group. It incorporates the fast search for essential subgroups of Gautam (\cite{Gau26}) and replaces the fusion graph of \cite{PS21} by a lazy, graph free computation. \mbox{}}\\[1cm]
{\small

\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Introduction}}\label{intro}

\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Fusion systems}}\logpage{[ 1, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X78B9FA547D3B76E6}{}
{
 

 Let $S$ be a finite $p$-group. A \emph{fusion system} on $S$ is a category $F$ whose objects are the subgroups of $S$ and whose morphisms $Hom_F(P,Q)$ are injective group homomorphisms containing all those induced by conjugation
in $S$, such that every morphism factors as an isomorphism followed by an inclusion.
The fusion system \emph{generated} by subgroups $A_i \le Aut(E_i)$ ($E_i \le S$) is the smallest fusion system containing them. By the
Alperin{\textendash}Goldschmidt theorem a saturated fusion system is generated
by $Aut_F(S)$ together with the groups $Aut_F(E)$, $E$ running through representatives of the $F$-conjugacy classes of \emph{essential} subgroups (the fully normalized $F$-centric subgroups $E$ for which $Out_F(E)$ has a strongly $p$-embedded subgroup). 

 In this package a fusion system is therefore given by the data 
\begin{itemize}
\item $S$, a $p$-group given as a pc group,
\item automorphisms of $S$ which together with $Inn(S)$ generate $Aut_F(S)$,
\item a list of subgroups $E_1,\dots,E_k$ of $S$ (the essential subgroups) and, for each of them, a list of automorphisms
generating $Aut_F(E_i)$.
\end{itemize}
 The fusion system is the one generated by these groups; it is not assumed to
be saturated. Whether it is saturated is decided by \texttt{IsSaturated} (\ref{IsSaturated}). }

 
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Overview of the algorithms}}\logpage{[ 1, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X7BA6CDCD7AF21D61}{}
{
 

 \emph{Essential subgroups.} By \cite[Theorem 3.6]{Gau26} every essential subgroup of a saturated fusion system on $S$ is $S$-conjugate to one of the subgroups $C_S(xA/A)$, where $A$ runs through the terms of a central series of $S$ with factors of order $p$ refining the lower central series and contained in $[S,S]$, and $xA$ through the elements of order $p$ of $S/A$. These candidates are filtered with the tests of \cite{PS21}; all tests are invariant under $Aut(S)$ and the expensive ones (which need $Aut(P)$) are applied once per $Aut(S)$-orbit. The subgroup lattice of $S$ is never computed. 

 \emph{Automorphism groups.} Automorphism groups of $p$-groups are computed with the package \textsf{autpgrp}. If $Aut(P)$ is soluble all computations with its subgroups take place in the pc group
returned by \texttt{PcGroupAutPGroup}; otherwise a permutation representation is used. 

 \emph{Fusion.} Let $B = Aut_F(S) \ltimes S$ and let $C$ be a $p'$-complement of $Inn(S)$ in $Aut_F(S)$. Every isomorphism in $F$ is a composite of restrictions of elements of $Aut_F(S)$ and of $Aut_F(E_i^s)$, $s \in S$. The $S$-conjugacy classes of subgroups form the nodes of a graph which is built
lazily: at a node with representative $R$ and for every $S$-conjugate $E^s$ of an essential subgroup containing $R$ we record the Schreier graph of the orbit of $R$ under $Aut_F(E^s)$, with the arrows conjugated into the class representatives, and the arrows $R \to c(R)$ for the generators $c$ of $C$. By the Reidemeister{\textendash}Schreier procedure for groupoids the $F$-class of $R$ is the connected component of its node and $Aut_F(R)$ is generated by the conjugates of the groups $Aut_S(X)$, $X$ a node of the component, and the loops of the component. 

 \emph{Saturation.} By \cite[Theorem 2.3]{PS21} (which rests on \cite[Theorem 2.2]{BCGLO05}) a fusion system generated by $Aut_F(S)$ and the automizers of $F$-centric subgroups is saturated if and only if $Inn(S)$ is a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $Aut_F(S)$, every fully normalized $F$-centric subgroup $P$ is fully automized, and every fully normalized $F$-centric $F$-radical $P$ has the \emph{surjectivity property}: for all $P < V \le N_S(P)$ the restriction map $N_{Aut_F(V)}(P) \to N_{Aut_F(P)}(Aut_V(P))$ is surjective. Let $T$ be the set of subgroups of $S$ contained in a $B$-conjugate of an essential subgroup. $T$ is closed under $F$-conjugacy and under taking subgroups, and for $P \notin T$ every $F$-morphism with source $P$ is the restriction of a conjugation by an element of $B$ (the automizers of the essential subgroups never apply). Hence the $F$-class of $P$, $Aut_F(P)$ and the extension condition at $P$ are those of the saturated fusion system $F_S(B)$, and the conditions hold. It therefore suffices to run the test over the $F$-classes of the $S$-centric subgroups of the essential subgroups. These are found from the
subgroup lattices of the groups $E_i/Z(E_i)$, their $F$-classes and automizers from the lazy graph. A class is only expanded as far
as it is needed: the test abandons the $F$-class of an essential subgroup, or of an $S$-centric subgroup of one, at the first member which is not $S$-centric or has a larger normalizer in $S$, as such a member already decides the condition in question. (For a candidate
system which is far from saturated such a class may be enormous, for instance
when a subgroup of an abelian essential subgroup with a large automizer lies
in it, while its first bad member is found at once.) This is how the package
avoids the fusion graph of \cite{PS21}, whose construction (the subgroup lattice of $S$ up to $B$-conjugacy and the $Aut_F(E)$-orbits of all subgroups of all essential subgroups) is the most expensive
part of the original implementation. 

 \emph{Classification.} \texttt{AllFusionSystems} (\ref{AllFusionSystems}) follows \cite[Section 4]{PS21}: for each $p'$-subgroup $K$ of $Aut(S)$ up to conjugacy ($Aut_F(S) = Inn(S) \rtimes K$) the proto-essential subgroups are grouped into $B$-classes; the candidates for $Aut_F(P)$ are the subgroups $A$ of $Aut(P)$ with $Aut_S(P)$ as Sylow $p$-subgroup and $A/Inn(P)$ having a strongly $p$-embedded subgroup, one for each $Aut(P)$-class (all conjugates of such a subgroup containing $Aut_S(P)$ as a Sylow $p$-subgroup are conjugate under $N_{Aut(P)}(Aut_S(P))$), expanded to the conjugates whose Sylow normalizer contains $Aut_{N_B(P)}(P)$, with equality when $N_S(P)$ lies in no $B$-conjugate of a proto-essential subgroup; the subsets of proto-essentials and
the assignments of automizers are run through up to the action of $N_{Aut(S)}(Aut_F(S))$; the resulting systems are tested for $O^p(F)=F$, $O_p(F)=1$ and saturation and finally reduced up to isomorphism. The automizer candidates
are enumerated by the cyclic extension method with the hereditary bound $|H|_p \le |Out_S(P)|$; this is complete whenever GAP can handle the subgroup lattice of $Out(P)$. For elementary abelian $P$ with a huge $Out(P) = GL(n,p)$ the package falls back to the monomial groups of the $Aut_S(P)$-invariant frames (and reports this through \texttt{InfoFusionSystems} (\ref{InfoFusionSystems})), or uses candidates supplied by the user through the option \texttt{candidates}. }

 }

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{FusionSystem}}
\logpage{[ 2, 1, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X85E0AA3685192CC5}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FusionSystem({\mdseries\slshape S, autSgens, essentials, essautos})\index{FusionSystem@\texttt{FusionSystem}}
\label{FusionSystem}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns the fusion system on the pc group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} generated by $Inn(S)$, the automorphisms in the list \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape autSgens}} (or the group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape autSgens}} of automorphisms of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}), and the automorphisms in \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape essautos}}\texttt{[i]} of the subgroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape essentials}}\texttt{[i]} of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S := ExtraspecialGroup( 27, 3 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@E := First( MaximalSubgroups( S ), M -> IsElementaryAbelian( M ) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@A := AutomorphismGroup( E );;  n := NiceMonomorphism( A );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@sl := List( GeneratorsOfGroup( DerivedSubgroup( Image( n ) ) ),|
  !gapprompt@>| !gapinput@               x -> PreImagesRepresentative( n, x ) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@F := FusionSystem( S, [], [ E ], [ sl ] );|
  <fusion system on a group of order 3^3 with 1 essential classes>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsSaturated( F );|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{GroupFusionSystem (for a group and a prime)}}
\logpage{[ 2, 1, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7DC5D03C842402A3}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GroupFusionSystem({\mdseries\slshape G, p[, opts]})\index{GroupFusionSystem@\texttt{GroupFusionSystem}!for a group and a prime}
\label{GroupFusionSystem:for a group and a prime}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{GroupFusionSystem({\mdseries\slshape G, S[, opts]})\index{GroupFusionSystem@\texttt{GroupFusionSystem}!for a group and a Sylow subgroup}
\label{GroupFusionSystem:for a group and a Sylow subgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns the fusion system $F_S(G)$ of the finite group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} on a Sylow \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}-subgroup \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}. The underlying group of the result is the pc group \texttt{Image( IsomorphismPcGroup( S ) )}; the isomorphism is stored in the component \texttt{F!.iso} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} is the value of the attribute \texttt{FusionSystemGroup}. The essential subgroups are searched among the candidates of Gautam's
theorem; with \texttt{opts := rec( exhaustive := true )} all $S$-centric subgroups are examined instead. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@F := GroupFusionSystem( PSU( 4, 3 ), 3 );|
  <fusion system on a group of order 3^6 with 2 essential classes>
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@OutFSOrder( F );  List( EssentialSubgroups( F ), Size );|
  4
  [ 243, 81 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@List( EssentialAutomizers( F ), Size );|
  [ 3888, 360 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Saturation, $O_p(F)$ and the focal subgroup}}\logpage{[ 2, 3, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8493B5977D06AD52}{}
{
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsSaturated}}
\logpage{[ 2, 3, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X81CCD9A88127E549}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsSaturated({\mdseries\slshape F})\index{IsSaturated@\texttt{IsSaturated}}
\label{IsSaturated}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{FS{\textunderscore}IsSaturatedWithReason({\mdseries\slshape F})\index{FS{\textunderscore}IsSaturatedWithReason@\texttt{FS{\textunderscore}}\-\texttt{Is}\-\texttt{Saturated}\-\texttt{With}\-\texttt{Reason}}
\label{FSuScoreIsSaturatedWithReason}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 whether the fusion system \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} is saturated; the second function returns \texttt{[ true ]} or \texttt{[ false, reason ]}. The test is the one described in Chapter \ref{intro}. The essential subgroups of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} are required to be $F$-centric and fully normalized (for the fusion system to be saturated with
these essential subgroups); if this fails the result is \texttt{false}. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@F := GroupFusionSystem( PSL( 3, 3 ), 3 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FS_IsSaturatedWithReason( F );|
  [ true ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S := UnderlyingGroup( F );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@F1 := FusionSystem( S, [], [ EssentialSubgroups( F )[1] ], [ EssentialAutomizers( F )[1] ] );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@FS_IsSaturatedWithReason( F1 );|
  [ false, "the surjectivity property fails at a subgroup of order 9" ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

\label{IsPPerfectFusionSystem}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (property)}}\\


 \texttt{OpF( F )} is the largest subgroup of $S$ normal in $S$, contained in all essential subgroups and invariant under $Aut_F(S)$ and all $Aut_F(E_i)$; for saturated \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F}} this is $O_p(F)$. \texttt{FocalSubgroup( F )} is $\langle [S, Aut_F(S)], [E_i, Aut_F(E_i)] \rangle$, which is the focal subgroup of a saturated fusion system; $O^p(F) = F$ iff it is all of $S$. }

 }

 
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Isomorphism}}\logpage{[ 2, 4, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X80F38E797C303471}{}
{
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{IsIsomorphicFusionSystems}}
\logpage{[ 2, 4, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X87BD925E80E6358B}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsIsomorphicFusionSystems({\mdseries\slshape F1, F2})\index{IsIsomorphicFusionSystems@\texttt{IsIsomorphicFusionSystems}}
\label{IsIsomorphicFusionSystems}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{IsomorphismFusionSystems({\mdseries\slshape F1, F2})\index{IsomorphismFusionSystems@\texttt{IsomorphismFusionSystems}}
\label{IsomorphismFusionSystems}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (operation)}}\\


 whether there is an isomorphism $\alpha: S_1 \to S_2$ carrying \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F1}} onto \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F2}}, i.e. carrying the generating data of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F1}} into \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F2}} and vice versa; the second function returns such an isomorphism or \texttt{fail}. If \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F1}} and \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape F2}} live on the same group $S$, $\alpha$ is searched in $Aut(S)$; otherwise an isomorphism of the groups is computed first. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@F1 := GroupFusionSystem( PSL( 3, 3 ), 3 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@F2 := GroupFusionSystem( MathieuGroup( 12 ), 3 );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@IsIsomorphicFusionSystems( F1, F2 );|
  false
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 }

 }

 
\chapter{\textcolor{Chapter }{Classification}}\label{classify}
\logpage{[ 3, 0, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X8053C9E57C4C5F94}{}
{
 
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{Essential subgroups and their automizers}}\logpage{[ 3, 1, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X822129EC817F68C9}{}
{
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{RefinedLowerCentralSeries}}
\logpage{[ 3, 1, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X83C1B9807EB1C724}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{RefinedLowerCentralSeries({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{RefinedLowerCentralSeries@\texttt{RefinedLowerCentralSeries}}
\label{RefinedLowerCentralSeries}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\
\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{CentralSeriesCentralizers({\mdseries\slshape S})\index{CentralSeriesCentralizers@\texttt{CentralSeriesCentralizers}}
\label{CentralSeriesCentralizers}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 a central series of the $p$-group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}} with all factors of order $p$ refining the lower central series, and the list of the subgroups $C_S(xA/A)$ of Gautam's theorem. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ProtoEssentialSubgroups}}
\logpage{[ 3, 1, 2 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7A73BA547808B347}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ProtoEssentialSubgroups({\mdseries\slshape S[, opts]})\index{ProtoEssentialSubgroups@\texttt{ProtoEssentialSubgroups}}
\label{ProtoEssentialSubgroups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns a record with components \texttt{autreps} (representatives of the $Aut(S)$-classes of proto-essential subgroups), \texttt{sreps} (representatives of their $S$-classes), \texttt{label} and \texttt{path} (\texttt{sreps[i]} is the image of \texttt{autreps[label[i]]} under the automorphism \texttt{path[i][1]} conjugated by \texttt{path[i][2]}). With \texttt{opts := rec( exhaustive := true )} all $S$-centric subgroups are examined instead of Gautam's candidates. 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@S := SylowSubgroup( PSU( 4, 3 ), 3 );;  S := Image( IsomorphismPcGroup( S ) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@r := ProtoEssentialSubgroups( S );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@List( r.autreps, Size );|
  [ 243, 81 ]
\end{Verbatim}
 }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{ProtoEssentialAutomizerCandidates}}
\logpage{[ 3, 1, 3 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X825D202F8120CB37}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{ProtoEssentialAutomizerCandidates({\mdseries\slshape S, P[, opts]})\index{ProtoEssentialAutomizerCandidates@\texttt{ProtoEssentialAutomizerCandidates}}
\label{ProtoEssentialAutomizerCandidates}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 the subgroups $A$ of $Aut(P)$ (as subgroups of the model group of \texttt{FS{\textunderscore}AutHandle( P )}) containing $Inn(P)$ with $Aut_S(P)$ as Sylow $p$-subgroup and with $A/Inn(P)$ having a strongly $p$-embedded subgroup, one for each $Aut(P)$-class. \texttt{opts.candidates} may be a function \texttt{(S, P)} returning lists of automorphisms (or model subgroups) to be used instead. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{BorelSubgroups}}
\logpage{[ 3, 1, 4 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X787ED1557EFD3831}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{BorelSubgroups({\mdseries\slshape S[, orders]})\index{BorelSubgroups@\texttt{BorelSubgroups}}
\label{BorelSubgroups}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 the $p'$-subgroups $K$ of $Aut(S)$ up to conjugacy, as records with components \texttt{model} and \texttt{gens} (the generators as automorphisms of \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}); $Inn(S) \rtimes K$ runs through the possibilities for $Aut_F(S)$. }

 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{HasStronglyPEmbeddedSubgroup}}
\logpage{[ 3, 1, 5 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X78E535967D9A301C}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{HasStronglyPEmbeddedSubgroup({\mdseries\slshape G, p})\index{HasStronglyPEmbeddedSubgroup@\texttt{HasStronglyPEmbeddedSubgroup}}
\label{HasStronglyPEmbeddedSubgroup}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 whether the finite group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape G}} has a strongly \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape p}}-embedded subgroup: with $T$ a Sylow $p$-subgroup this is the case iff $\langle N_G(T), N_G(Q) : Q \le T, |Q| = p \rangle \ne G$. }

 }

 
\section{\textcolor{Chapter }{All saturated fusion systems on a $p$-group}}\logpage{[ 3, 2, 0 ]}
\hyperdef{L}{X781E645B7BA9B89B}{}
{
 

\subsection{\textcolor{Chapter }{AllFusionSystems}}
\logpage{[ 3, 2, 1 ]}\nobreak
\hyperdef{L}{X7B24A39A804E21C2}{}
{\noindent\textcolor{FuncColor}{$\triangleright$\enspace\texttt{AllFusionSystems({\mdseries\slshape S[, opts]})\index{AllFusionSystems@\texttt{AllFusionSystems}}
\label{AllFusionSystems}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (function)}}\\


 returns a list of representatives of the isomorphism classes of saturated
fusion systems on the pc group \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape S}}, by default those with $O_p(F) = 1$ and $O^p(F) = F$. The optional record \mbox{\texttt{\mdseries\slshape opts}} may have the components \texttt{OpTriv} (default \texttt{true}), \texttt{pPerfect} (default \texttt{true}), \texttt{OutFSOrders} (a list of admissible orders of $Out_F(S)$), \texttt{exhaustive} (default \texttt{false}) and \texttt{candidates} (a function supplying automizer candidates, see \texttt{ProtoEssentialAutomizerCandidates} (\ref{ProtoEssentialAutomizerCandidates})). Progress is reported at levels 1 and 2 of \texttt{InfoFusionSystems} (\ref{InfoFusionSystems}). 
\begin{Verbatim}[commandchars=!@|,fontsize=\small,frame=single,label=Example]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@L := AllFusionSystems( ExtraspecialGroup( 27, 3 ) );;|
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Length( L );|
  4
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@SortedList( List( L, OutFSOrder ) );|
  [ 4, 8, 8, 16 ]
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@ForAny( L, F -> IsIsomorphicFusionSystems( F, GroupFusionSystem( PSL( 3, 3 ), 3 ) ) );|
  true
  !gapprompt@gap>| !gapinput@Length( AllFusionSystems( ExtraspecialGroup( 343, 7 ) ) );|
  13
\end{Verbatim}
 The last example recovers the classification of Ruiz and Viruel for $7^{1+2}_+$ (ten systems realized by finite groups and three exotic ones). }

\label{InfoFusionSystems}
}\hfill{\scriptsize (info class)}}\\


 the info class of the package. }

 }
